data.narrative:
Ouster is a publicly-traded semiconductor company founded by Angus Pacala, currently valued at $2.26B after raising $500M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers in Chips & Semiconductors—Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and Aeva Technologies—alongside 8 additional private frontier-tech companies in the sector.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Across the 3 same-sector, same-stage public comparables, the median valuation stands at $35.8B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Aeva Technologies) to $39.2B (Cerebras). This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneous valuations typical of early-stage semiconductor innovators. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 20.4x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied without Ouster's disclosed revenue.

The single-method triangulation yields a narrow implied range of $30.4B (low) to $41.2B (high), centered on $35.8B. The current market valuation of $2.26B sits substantially below this peer-median estimate. Key uncertainties include revenue scale, margin trajectory, and whether Ouster's technology differentiation justifies valuation parity with higher-valued peers like Cerebras. The wide dispersion within the peer set ($1.1B–$39.2B) signals that sector fundamentals alone do not determine valuation; customer concentration, capital intensity, and technical risk play material roles.
